title: modernize-private-eks-controlplane-terraform-module-bootstrap
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a next-generation Terraform module to provision Redwood Private control plane (EKS) clusters with upgrade-safe primitives, robust preflight checks, and programmable health checks. The current bootstrap module is brittle during cluster upgrades and doesn't provide atomic, auditable steps for control plane lifecycle. This ticket scopes a production-ready module that: 1) creates the EKS control plane and required infra (VPC, subnets, NAT, route tables, IAM roles, OIDC provider), 2) codifies preflight validations to fail early, 3) provides clearly versioned outputs and semantic versioning for module releases, 4) supports in-place upgrades and a blue/green canary workflow implemented at a higher orchestration layer, 5) exposes health endpoints and metrics sinks used by Console for SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Module successfully provisions an EKS control plane and minimal nodegroup in a dev account using a single terraform apply. 2) Preflight checks detect common misconfigurations (CIDR overlap, missing KMS key, insufficient IAM permissions) and return actionable error messages. 3) Module exposes outputs (cluster_name, kubeconfig_secret_arn, eks_oidc_provider_arn, controlplane_state_key) and tags resources with standardized tags. 4) CI job can create ephemeral clusters using the module, run smoke tests (kubectl get nodes, deploy tiny workload, verify ServiceAccount OIDC integration) and destroy resources without leaks. 5) Upgrade playbook documented and tested in staging: control plane minor version bump with zero-control-plane downtime in at least one canary deployment. 6) Healthcheck hooks (api_version, apiserver_latency_p50/p95, kube_apiserver_ready) are present as module-local CloudWatch metrics or exported Prometheus metrics for Console ingestion.
implementation_notes:
- Split the module into clear submodules: networking, iam, eks_controlplane, addons_bootstrap, and observability. Each submodule must be independently testable.
- Use the upstream terraform-aws-eks module as a reference but avoid tight coupling; implement our opinionated defaults (OIDC provider creation idempotent, managed nodegroups optional, tags and naming conventions matching Redwood standards).
- Provide a 'preflight' terraform plan wrapper: a lightweight validation step (python script invoked in CI) that validates input variables, checks account-level permissions via STS, verifies Route53 private zones and KMS key access.
- Add lifecycle rules and replacement protection where appropriate (for example, controlplane security group changes should require explicit approval via a variable).
- Output a terraform state key path variable and require backend locking to support cross-account runs.
- Document recommended upgrade pattern: create parallel cluster for major upgrades or follow rolling minor upgrade strategy with canary nodegroups.
- Make module inputs backward-compatible: introduce 'deprecated' input names mapped to new names for two releases before removal.
- Add an example 'canary_rollout' wrapper (outside module) that demonstrates traffic shifting between clusters using Route53 weighted records.
testing_plan:
- CI: ephemeral cluster tests run on PRs to module repo using dedicated AWS account; steps: terraform init/apply -> run smoke tests (kube-apiserver readiness, SA OIDC token minting, coreDNS resolution) -> deploy sample app -> load test control plane endpoints at 50 RPS for 5 minutes -> terraform destroy.
- E2E: staging run where we upgrade a test cluster from 1.x -> 1.y using the new module; validate rollback path by intentionally failing addon upgrade and observing canary fallback.
- Chaos: run fault injection (control plane API latency simulation and k8s node termination) and verify observability alerts trigger and that autoscaling/eviction policies behave.
- Security: run terraform validate with SNYK and check IAM policy least-privilege through an automated policy review tool.
- Perf benchmark: measure first-packet latency and list/watch latencies pre/post upgrade to detect regressions.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge v2 module behind a feature flag and use it for dev ephemeral clusters only. 2) Run a small set of production-like staging clusters for 2 weeks and validate health metrics; iterate on observability. 3) Execute a canary upgrade on a single customer-simulated cluster using DNS weight shift (10% traffic for 1 hour, then 50% for 2 hours, then 100%); monitor Console SLOs. 4) If metrics pass, schedule tenant clusters upgrade by risk band; provide rollback runbook to Service Reliability. 5) Announce change and module semver v2.0.0 in release notes and update onboarding docs.
